content:
Congratulations to Drive Auto Repair for beating Motiv8 16-5. Real impressive, boys. You beat a team whose name is literally a motivational poster at a dentist's office. Pop the champagne. Call ESPN. Alert the media. A bunch of grown men with knee braces scored 16 runs against what appeared to be a team that carpooled from a fantasy football draft.

Coach Ranney drew up the game plan on a napkin at Waffle House and somehow it worked. The offense came out swinging like they all had outstanding warrants. The defense? Let's just say the errors weren't tracked because nobody wanted to do that much math.

Meanwhile, half the lineup can't touch their toes but swears they're "warming up" every Monday at 7:55 PM. The dugout smells like Bengay and bad decisions. One of you brought a lawn chair. You know who you are.

Rocket Power dropped 34 on the Dirt Dawgs, so let's not get too comfortable. Drive's 16 runs look cute next to that. That's like bragging about your Honda Civic at a Ferrari dealership — which, given the team name, is painfully on brand.

Next week: Flamingos. If you lose to a team called the Flamingos, every single one of you owes the group chat a pink jersey selfie. No exceptions. See you Monday. ⚾

Well, Drive Auto Repair finally lost a game. And not just any loss — a 20-8 dismantling at the hands of Rocket Power that looked less like a softball game and more like a hostage situation. The mercy rule was sitting at the bar across the street wondering why nobody invited it. Twenty runs. Twelve hits given up. The defense was so porous you could've watered a lawn through it.

Coach Ranney's pre-game speech was reportedly "don't embarrass the team in front of the league leaders" and gentlemen, you found a creative workaround. Rocket Power scored more runs in this single game than Drive scored in the entire previous WEEK. They didn't beat us, they CHARGED us — Rocket Power, get it? — like an Uber surge price after a Taylor Swift concert.

The offense managed 8 whole runs on 11 hits, which sounds respectable until you realize we drew exactly ONE walk all night. One. Uno. The entire team had the patience of a toddler at a candy store. Pitchers were lobbing meatballs at eye level and we were swinging like the ball owed us money. Special shoutout to Matthew, who went 0-for-2 with TWO outs and somehow still drove in a run — that's not a stat line, that's a magic trick.

Brad continues his audition for the "Most Hits By A Guy Who Looks Lost At The Plate" award, going 1-for-3 with a double and now sporting a beautiful .364 average. Brad, brother, the hits are coming, but it's giving "swung at it with his eyes closed and got lucky." Meanwhile Luc went 2-for-3 to push his season line to .467/.467/.467 — the rare slash where every number is the same, like he's a robot that was programmed for exactly one outcome and refuses to deviate.

The bright spot? Peter went deep AGAIN — that's 3 HRs in 4 games for the player-coach, who is now slashing .846/.857/1.692. The man is hitting like he's playing a different sport. Doug also drew 2 BB in his cleanup spot... wait, Doug bats cleanup? DOUG BATS CLEANUP? The man has 4 hits all season and 0 RBI. That's not a cleanup hitter, that's a guy who walks into the kitchen at midnight and forgets why he's there.

Welcome to Jackson, who made his Drive debut with a 1-for-2 night. Jackson, here's some advice: run. Run while you can. We are 3-1 but trending in the wrong direction and the schedule does not get easier. Mitchell — sorry, MITCH — also returned from his Game 2 sabbatical to go 1-for-1 with a sac and an RBI, proving once again that the only way to maintain a perfect season is to play exactly half of it.

Next week: Spring Break. Use the week off to learn what a strike zone looks like. Then it's Motiv8 in Week 7, who you already curb-stomped in Week 1. Don't get cute. Don't get fancy. Just remember that even Rocket Power had to lose eventually — to someone — and right now Drive is the team that gets in the way of someone else's highlight reel. Let's not be that team again. ⚾

Let me set the scene. Top of the 4th inning. Drive is DOWN 11-6 to Motiv8. MOTIV8. The team you beat 16-5 six weeks ago. The clock is ticking and your season's about to go in the dumpster behind HP2. And then Drive dropped TEN runs in a single half-inning to go up 16-11, survived Motiv8 answering with 4 in the bottom, and escaped with a 16-15 win in 4 innings. That's not a comeback. That's a jailbreak with witnesses.

First, the scene of the crime. Drive gave up 11 runs in the first three innings to MOTIV8. Eleven. To the team whose name is literally a motivational poster at a dentist's office. The defense was out there letting balls through like a colander with good intentions. Four in the first, six in the second — by the end of the 2nd Motiv8 was up 10-1 and their bench was talking smack in complete sentences.

Now let's talk lineup, because Austin C made the card this week and we need to have a conversation. Doug batting leadoff went 1-for-4 with three outs. Mitch batting 2nd went 0-for-4 with four outs. The 1-2 spots combined to go 1-for-8 with zero extra base hits in a game Drive won by one run. Fellas. FELLAS. Mitch, my guy, you made an out in every single at-bat in a game your team gave up 15 — you are the human embodiment of the phrase "not helping." Doug had exactly as many hits as my left shoe.

And here's the real crime: Peter is batting 3rd. Peter — the guy currently slashing .813/.824/1.688 for a 2.512 OPS, leading the team in every single offensive category — is hitting BEHIND Mitch, who is slashing .444/.444/.444. Austin, buddy, modern lineup theory says your best hitter bats second. Every analyst in the sport agrees on this. Peter went 2-for-3 with a double, a triple, and 2 RBI last night and he was doing it AFTER watching Mitch walk back to the dugout four straight times. Move Peter to the 2-hole and drop Mitch to 7 or lower until he remembers which end of the bat to hold. This isn't favoritism, this is math.

Then the 4th inning happened. Ten runs. TEN. The same Drive lineup that spent three innings looking like they'd never held a bat before suddenly turned into the 1927 Yankees for 15 minutes. Jackson went 3-for-3 with TWO doubles and 4 RBI batting EIGHTH, Luc launched the only home run of the night batting TENTH with 3 RBI, and Brad went a perfect 3-for-3 with a double batting ELEVENTH. The 8, 10, and 11 holes combined for 8 hits, a homer, and 7 RBI. Austin, you buried your three hottest bats at the bottom of the order and they still dragged you across the finish line. That's not a lineup, that's a witness protection program.

Quiet credit to the middle: Smitty went 2-for-2 with a sacrifice in the 4-hole, Max went 2-for-2 with a walk batting 5th, and Jason made his Drive debut batting 6th and went 1-for-2 with a walk, a run scored, and an RBI — welcome to Drive, Jason, the hazing is you have to read this roast every week and pretend it's funny. Ryan hit 7th and ripped a double to help ignite the rally. That middle chunk from 3 through 7 is actually mashing; it's the top and the bookends you hid at the bottom that need fixing.

Final: 16-15 in 4 innings, saved by a 10-run explosion from a backwards lineup card, with the top two hitters contributing roughly the same amount of offense as the chalk bucket. Next Monday: Flamingos at 9 PM, home. Austin — put Peter at 2, drop Mitch, let Jackson hit higher than 8. Doug and Mitch — hit the ball or start warming up pink jerseys. And for the love of God, somebody catch a softball on defense. See you Monday. ⚾

We lost 22-21 to the Flamingos. A team named after the plastic lawn ornament sitting in your grandma's front yard. By one run. In a game we lost by giving up eight runs in the first inning before half the lineup had located their glove. The 10-run rally in the second wasn't a comeback, gentlemen, it was a receipt — mathematical proof we could've won this if we'd bothered showing up on time.

The first-inning defense looked like a community theater production of "softball." Ground balls became adventures. Routine flies became suspense films. The Flamingos didn't earn those eight runs — we catered them, plated them, and picked up the tab. If "lots of errors" were a stat we tracked per player, half of you would owe the scorekeeper a drink.

Austin W — you struck out LOOKING. In slow-pitch softball. The pitch comes in on an 8-foot rainbow arc at the approximate speed of a kid learning to ride a bike. You had time to see it, time it, write a short essay about it, and still swing. You chose violence against yourself instead. Sure, you hit a homer earlier — which somehow makes it worse, because now we know you CAN hit, you just opted not to.

And then there's Coach Ranney — 4-for-4, grand slam, 5 RBI — dragging the rest of the lineup around like a hostage. Peter single-handedly drove in a quarter of the team's runs. The lineup he wrote is beating the lineup he's playing with. Meanwhile, Doug hit a SAC FLY in a slugfest — which, fine, it drove in a run, we appreciate you Doug. But Doug, buddy, we lost by ONE. ONE RUN. One more foot of trajectory and that ball leaves the yard. Jackson collected three more singles like he's scared of second base. Smitty made two outs in four tries and called it a day.

Next week: Dirt Dawgs at HP2, our house. They got run-ruled 34-13 by Rocket Power earlier this season, so if Drive drops this one, we should forfeit the rest of the season and take up pickleball like the suburban dads we clearly are. Show up warm. Field the ball. Swing the bat. It's not complicated. ⚾

Eighteen runs on the Dirt Dawgs. Last week they put 25 on us and this week we put 18 on them — apparently the entire league is allergic to playing defense two weeks in a row. Revenge served cold, in five innings, with a side of mercy rule. The Dirt Dawgs showed up looking like guys who already had Tuesday's hangover scheduled.

Doug went 4-for-4 — all singles — like he just unlocked a new bat at Dick's and refuses to swing for anything past the infield. Four hits, ONE run scored. Bro you're a station-to-station guy in a slow-pitch league where the bases are 70 feet apart. Bunting would be more aggressive. Meanwhile Max also went 4-for-4 with an actual triple and crossed the plate four times because he understands that hits are supposed to lead to runs.

Mitch and Austin W tied for MVP of the night — both 3-for-4 with a homer and 4 RBIs. Luc went 2-for-4 but somehow drove in 5 runs, which means he's officially the most efficient bat on the team and also the only one who shows up when the bases are loaded. Smitty got on base twice, scored once, and added another walk to his Hall of Fame patience tour.

And then there's Jackson — 1-for-4 with 3 outs, batting like the ball personally insulted his mother. Ryan got 2 hits and somehow scored ZERO runs, which is a special kind of art form. You need a courtesy runner for yourself at this point. Brad: 3 singles, 0 RBIs, 1 run — the human equivalent of a parked Honda Civic with the engine running.

And where the hell was Coach Ranney? The team's leading hitter (.792, 5 HR) sat out the game where we put up 18 runs on a divisional rival the week before playoffs. Either he's resting his hammies for the postseason or he saw the Rocket Power 8-0 record and developed mysterious flu symptoms. We see you, Peter.

Speaking of which — Rocket Power finished 8-0. Eight. And. Zero. They've outscored everyone like it's batting practice. Drive locks in the 2-seed, gets a bye to Round 2, and waits for whoever crawls out of HS Legends vs Flamingos (4 vs 5, both 3-5, both auditioning for the worst-team-to-make-the-playoffs trophy). Win that and we get Rocket Power in the championship. Wash the jerseys, ice the knees, and pray nobody pulls a hamstring getting out of the truck. Playoffs start 5/11. ⚾
